propositions: When two agents race on the same parent and different children in a same-tracker serialized scenario, the parent lock ensures one agent's cascade claim wins; the other agent should proceed to claim its child independently without cascading the already-in-progress parent.

In offline two-clone scenarios where both clones independently claim an open parent and child(ren), fork resolution by UUID tie-break must converge deterministically per ticket, so a child's winner may differ from its parent's winner if they were both claimed concurrently.

Losing agents' already-written claims (parent and/or child) must remain in place orphaned under their assignee and not be rolled back; the status fork resolution is signaled via STATUS_FORK_RESOLVED on affected tickets.

The current claim.py implementation contains a TOCTOU race where a stale open-state read drives the cascade decision, causing ConcurrencyMismatch on the locked parent claim to abort the entire child claim; this must be fixed to treat a no-longer-open parent as benign and proceed to claim the child.
Policy documentation for both sub-cases (same-tracker serialized and two-clone offline) must be committed to concurrency.md or CLAUDE.md before corresponding tests assert the behavior.
